lines: New Players? tab (after FAQ): the six classes with their weapons and starting gems, the game rules you meet first, a guide to every tab of this site, and the 19 builds the game's own Guide (F1) suggests. Open any of them here as a plan: passive tree, Dragonling, skill with its supports and the item bases (the guide's rare items carry no stat lines, so the damage shown is lower than the guide's figure).

Unarmed attacks (no weapon in your main hand): the bare-fist base damage now grows with your level, as in the game. It was a fixed 12-27 Physical, so low-level characters were shown about 1.7x too much and level 100 characters about 0.6x too little. Game tests at levels 12 and 100 now match within 2-3%.

Facebreaker: tested in game. Its 500% more Physical damage only counts with nothing in your main hand; a claw or fist weapon there turns it off, even with Open Hand. A fist in the off hand is fine. The planner already worked this way.
Build Planner: with no character loaded, a Start fresh button starts a new plan from scratch (no code needed).
Home shows the landing page again when no character is loaded (it was blank since 25 Nov).

Configure Enemy: every curse now shows its own numbers. Woe of Entropy, Woe of Faltering, Woe of Rime, Sentence of Chains, Sentence of Rot and Unravel no longer show a raw {x}% or drop their slow and less-damage parts. The FAQ curse table adds Chaos damage taken and less damage dealt.

Guardians, corrected: a Woe and a Sentence both count on a Guardian and multiply, as Patch 84 says. Yesterday's change (only the bigger of the two) is undone: a game test on the Guardian Post read Death Sentence x1.33, Woe of Sundering x1.35 and both together x1.71.

Woes now count in full on a Guardian (they were counted at half). The same test showed Woe of Sundering at its full 36.5% on the Guardian Post. Every Woe build gains Guardian DPS; the resistance Woes lower resistance by their full amount there too.

Guardians: a Woe and a Sentence no longer multiply there. Only the bigger of the two counts, as the game's own data says (its Guardian rule is still switched on). Checked in the game on build 93: on a Guardian Post, Woe of Sundering next to Death Sentence added nothing. Builds with both lose Guardian DPS; a Woe on its own still counts at half its effect on a Guardian. The planner reads this rule from the game data, so it follows the game if the switch changes.

War Banner: Valour left blank now counts full Valour off a Guardian and none on a Guardian, where nothing dies near the banner (it used to count full Valour everywhere). Checked in the game on build 93: a banner on a Guardian Post gave 6% x its effect, no Valour. Also for a banner planted by an item or the tree. A Valour you type is used as typed.

Patch 94: Summon Skeletons, Summon Skeletal Mage and Raise Zombie now get their minions by gem level as the patch says (Skeletons 2, a 3rd at gem level 3, a 4th at 7; the 2nd Skeletal Mage at 10; Raise Zombie 1, the 2nd at 3). While fewer stand, each one deals more: as much as the count the gem reaches later (gem level 21 for Skeletons, 12 for the Mage, 23 for Zombies) divided by how many stand. Checked in the game on build 94: 3 Skeletons at gem level 5 each deal 4/3, a lone Skeleton pair at gem level 1 twice as much. From gem level 20 on, nothing changes.
Not checked yet: whether gem levels from supports or gear count toward these steps (the planner counts them), and whether extra minions from the tree or items lower the bonus (the planner says no).

Configure Enemy: a "Skill that shocks" picker (Auto, None, or one skill on your bar) chooses whose shock is counted. A Woe's Dread you type is now used as typed; leave it blank for the 10 it builds on a Rare or Guardian.
Recent Patch: Patch 94 in short.

Minions attack slower on the game's own sheet than the planner showed. Skeletons, Skeletal Mages, Zombies and golems now read 7 to 18% lower at normal minion speed, and up to about 40% lower for very fast armies (several speed supports plus speed gear). Checked in the game on build 93: Skeletons with no speed read one attack every 0.704 s (the planner had 0.642), a Skeletal Mage with two speed supports 0.590 s (0.530).

The rule behind it: an attack takes the longest of the minion's base pace, half of its attack animation, and the time until the blow lands, plus 0.06 s the game adds to every minion attack. Fast armies gain less from more minion speed than before.
Grave Call's 30% more damage and 20% more attack speed are now confirmed from the game; the speed part gives less on minions already held back by their attack animation.
Skeletal Mages follow every cast speed support on the summon: Spell Echo's 10% less cast speed now slows them (from the developer's rule file, not yet checked in game).
Not checked yet: the Holy Elemental and the companions keep their old pace.

Shocks that stack (Gathering Storm, Oath of the Rolling Thunder and other "your Shocks stack" lines) now count on a Guardian too, and their sizes add. Checked in the game on build 93; the old rule of one shock on a Guardian is gone.

With a stacking shock skill on your bar, the shocks of your other skills now sit next to its stacks and add (checked in the game: 3 shocks on a Guardian Post read 27% with the strongest at its 24% cap). Without one, your skills still share one shock, the strongest.

Static Build (each lightning hit adds 0.5% to the shock on a rare or Guardian) now grows only the strongest shock, as the game does, and counts the lightning hits of all your skills. A weaker new shock does not renew the grown one, so a skill with a low shock chance keeps the enemy shocked a little less of the time than before.

Consecrated Ground: every tick of its ground is counted, 10 hits a cast. It used to count as one hit, so its damage and the shock it lays for your other skills were far too low. Its 3 second cooldown no longer shortens with cast speed.
Curses on the enemy: each ticked curse now shows what its number is made of (Guardian share, curse effect, Dread, Mark effect).
Hunter's Marks: you can type more Marks than your own maximum to test; blank is still your maximum.

Support Tempering (game build 93, the Forge from Rupture Level 100) is counted. A tempered support with a less damage line loses part of it (2% more damage at level 5), one without gains a little more damage (0.5% at level 5), and its mana cost multiplier drops by up to 6 points.
The level is read from your save. To set it by hand, open a skill and use the Tempering row under its supports (0 to 5 per support).
Share links and plans carry the Tempering levels.

Game build 93: the six new crit ailment notables are counted (Butcher's Ledger, Honed Wound, Ripping Barbs, Kindled Heart, Searing Verdict, Hasty Rot). A critical strike's Bleeding, Ignite or Poison keeps 25 to 35% of the crit's extra damage.
Minion poison keeps its critical strike damage again: the game takes the crit out of your own Poison only. A small gain for most minion builds.
Necromancer: the two Oath seats renamed Mastery of the Reaping offer their Oaths again, with the four new ones (Reaper's Tithe, Grave Harvest, Rotting Edge, Wide Arc).
A note now says when a skill will not work with the weapon you hold (game build 93: no melee skills on a bow or wand, and bow skills need a bow). The damage is still shown.
Recent Patch: "In short" lines for game build 93.

Sparks: Convergence is counted again (one Spark skill on a Rare or Guardian: up to 50% faster strikes). Since the game data of build 92 the page had left it out, so a single Spark skill read about a third too low against a Rare or Guardian.
Mana: flat mana regeneration (Vow of Clarity) is now raised by your increased mana regeneration, as the game does.

Called Shot (game build 92): while the enemy holds all your Hunter's Marks, the hits of a skill with no Hunter's Mark support deal 15% more. Counted when your minions lay the Marks or Hunter's Mark is ticked at full in the curse list.

Elemental Echo (game build 92): against a Rare or Guardian your hits now leave an echo of each element they deal, so those echoes are counted without a tick (12% more of that element). Untick one to leave it out. The hit and panel numbers stay without them.
Oathwords on a low base: below the word's first power band, its power lines count at item level / word level (gem level lines in full).
Blood Ledger: a Slam implodes Entropy for 5% more, not 20% (game data 92).
Chill: any cold damage chills again, with no 25% cold share needed (the page had brought that floor back with game data 92).
Loot Filter: the game's new Clear preset is now among the game's own presets.

Two or more Spark skills on your bar (Ember, Rime, Venom, Storm): since game build 92 they share one Spark maximum, so against an enemy each now counts its part of it instead of a full set each. The skill panel number is unchanged, and one Spark skill alone is unchanged.
Curses: Hunter's Mark now counts the Marks you set (1.7% each, blank = full) and only raises hits; with a Hunter's Mark support on the skill too, only the bigger of the two counts.
War Banner: each Valour adds 0.5% more damage taken on top of its 6% (it used to raise the 6% by 0.5% a Valour).
Woe of Withering now raises your poison damage (its Poison line reached hits only). Woe of Sundering's Physical line now reaches bleeds too.
A Woe on a Guardian now says "x0.5 on a Guardian" next to its number.
Shock from your other skills: a skill whose Shocks stack (Living Storm) now counts all its stacks for your other skills, off Guardians. On a Guardian one shock counts, as before.

Cast on Crit with nothing linked is now cast by your main skill when it is an attack, else by your attack with the most damage on the bar. Any attack counts, Cyclone and other Movement attacks too, and a gem that is not on your bar no longer does.

EHP and Max hit: with a Guardian and its element picked in Configure Enemy, EHP is worked out against its crushing blow (two thirds physical, one third that element) instead of an even mix. The Max hit table gets a row for that blow.
Market: Copy mods copies the three mods worth the most to the character you have loaded (damage, and defence when Prioritize weighs it). With no character it copies the best-tier mods as before.

Item Simulator, Gear Set Sim and the tree optimizer: a Cast on Crit skill that counts by itself now adds its damage to your main skill instead of weighing as much as it. A small Cast on Crit spell no longer makes a much weaker weapon (a staff) come out on top.
New "Fortified stacks" box in Configure Enemy: type the stacks the game shows if you have more than your maximum Fortified lines give. 0 keeps the lines.

Spark skills strike again: since the 24 Nov game data, every Spark skill was simmed as one plain cast. Glacial Shards and Thunderfall get their spell lines back, Iaido Thrust its sheathe cut, Wind Vault its landing arrows, Lightning Arrow its return strike on a lone target, and Trap its re-arm time.
Unique lines follow the game's latest table (Cinderwick's strike rate is lower).
Channel Conduit: a channel that is not on your action bar no longer casts its linked spell; the spell uses its own supports.
A spell cast by a Channel Conduit now says so in its skill window, with a "Cast by hand" button. A support that cannot go into a skill says why.
Search box on every support picker (name or effect).
"Socket preset supports" for Heralds, Vows, Woes, Jarl's Roar, Sentences and movement skills; a new skill of these kinds gets them straight away.
"Packs and extras" and the other folded support groups stay open once you open them.
A new build starts at level 100, gem level 20 and all Dragonling points; lower them by hand.
New "Export for Oathfilter" button at the top of the Loot Filter tab and under your gear on the Character tab: copies a link with your worn gear for Oathfilter, demon_2m22's loot filter builder.
The sidebar now links to Oathfilter.
Energy Shield at the top of the page, in EHP and on the Advanced tab now counts your items' Base Grade and quality, their local % lines and "more" lines such as Vow of Warding. It read low before.
Evasion: the amount your level gives now matches the game (a little more below level 100).
Idol Sim and Gear Set Sim: a Vow on a red idol is never a +1 count line any more (+1 Ballista, Spark, Chain and the like). The game does not allow it, but the search put them there.
Idol Sim and Gear Set Sim: new box "Allow +1 count lines on idols", off by default. These Grand Idol lines are very rare drops, so the search leaves them out unless you tick it.
Save Creator: a copied build now gets the bonus passive points its tree needs. A full 128-point tree could come out with only 99 points in game.

Dragonling tree: the Dragon Ruptures box now follows the nodes you take. Taking a node past your points raises it (up to all 15) and refunding lowers it back, the way your level follows the passive tree's points. A crown is blocked only when it would not fit with all 15. (This went live with the last update.)
Recent Patch: the newest step is labelled Patch 91 + 92, because the public game data went from build 90 straight to 92. Its TLDR has "In short" lines that say which patch each change came with.
Recent Patch: game builds 89 and 90 are no longer listed twice.
Patch 91 and 92 rules that the game data did not carry by itself are now in the sim. They come from the developer's notes and rule files; none is checked in game yet, so tell us if one looks wrong.
Bina's Spotter's Helm: ramp up to 10% (patch 92, was 25%).
Ailment chance over 100%: each 1% over now gives 0.5% increased ailment damage (was 1%).

Kindled Remains: corpse bursts use the new shares (12.6% / 25.2% / 28.8% of corpse life by Rupture Level), grow with the skill's increased and more damage and with increased Corpse damage, and up to 3 corpses burst per hit. At high Rupture Levels it reads much lower than before.
Dual wielding: 25% more attack speed with a weapon in each hand (patch 92).
Hunter's Marks laid by minions count half: 0.85% each, 8.5% at 10 Marks (was 17%).
Minion mana: each kind of minion past the second makes every kind hold 25% more mana (patch 91).
Holy Elemental: your increased Holy damage lines now reach it.
Passive points: 5 more from Guardian kills at Rupture Level 105 to 145 (patch 91), so the most is 128 at level 100.
Best Rivenstone: gem level lines cost 4 Rivenstones (patch 92). One is picked only when you have that many, and it is weighed by its gain per stone.
Skill tree: Optimize tree, Plan tree and Plan next points work on a new plan once it has a skill (before, they did nothing), and say so when it has none.
Character tab: wear several Dwarven runes, one cell each, plus an empty cell to add another; the tree's Dwarven Sockets box follows how many you wear.

Many lines the sim used to leave out are now counted, as best guesses from their in-game text. Each one says so in the notes under the damage numbers; none is checked in game yet, so tell us if one looks wrong.

Lines with a condition now count: holding a Tome, wielding a Bow or Wand, unarmed (Facebreaker), skills that hit with both weapons, standing still (Anvil Stance, Hunter's Patience, The Last Square), and "below half life" lines with Scab of the Wound.

Dragonling nodes now counted: Mountain's Patience, Ancestral Echo, Sheathed Fury, Shaper of Flames, Deep Chill, Fault Lines, Jarl's Due, Thunderclap, Wound Echo, War Bringer, Culling Draw, Patient Host, March on the Sentenced.

Uniques now counted: The Reckoner's Wraps, Raijin's Fist and Moon-Leap Greaves (Fury), The Prismatic Codex, Mamushi Knuckles, Gravetithe, Jarlsbane, Mainspring Maul, The Mirror Oath, The Pilgrim's Pyre, Standard of the Last Legion, Gloomsilver Reliquary, Core-Splinter Idol.

Tree and minions: Hollow Crown (and The Keeper's Ember, Bone Choir Diadem), Covenant of Stone and Bone, Reaper's Due, Kindled Flesh, Storm Spotter, Wand Duelist, Standard of the Oath and Grave Standard (War Banner), Oathstone Ward, Sanctuary of Thought. Soul Rend on your bar now makes the enemy take 10% more from your minions.
Skill tree: lines the sim counts no longer show as "not counted", and defence or utility lines no longer show as not modelled.

Legion of One: a new "Legion of One kind" choice in Configure Enemy picks which of your summons stands. That kind gets the node's bonuses and your other summons count as 0 in every number (default: the strongest, as before).
Advanced tab: no longer goes blank when the main skill is a summon.
Character tab: a new Sim Idols button by the Fossil opens the Idol Sim in a window, so you can find and equip the best idols without leaving the tab.
Fury Unbottled (Brewmaw Oath): drinking a potion now spends the Fury you hold for more damage per charge, and those charges stop giving their own bonus while it lasts. It was missing from the sim.

Enemy settings are now kept when you reload the page: the enemy for every character, and curses, Vows, shocks and charges per character. A War Banner on your bar counts full Valour by default. "Reset to build defaults" puts them back.
New in the Item Simulator: Idol Sim, the Gear Set Sim for idols only. It finds the best idols for your skill and a Fossil layout they fit in; Equip puts them on.
Gear Set Sim: idol rows now have an Equip button too.
The Chill note now says when your chill effect is already past the 50% cap, which is why an Oath like the Long Winter can show +0%.
Dragonling heat map: nodes for your own hits (not totems) are no longer coloured by the bow lines on the path to them.

Hunter's Marks now raise hits only, not damage over time, as in the game (checked in game on poison ticks; Bleeding and Ignite are taken to follow). Skills with Marks and a damage over time part read lower.
Trap Support: traps re-arm after about a second again. The sim had fallen back to 2.5 seconds when patch 90 reworded the support's text, so skills thrown as a Trap read higher.
Spell Echo no longer repeats a toggle (Orbiting Hammers, Unholy Void, Pyre of Faith). The sim had started counting those repeats again with the same patch 90 text change.
Orbiting Hammers and Hammerstorm: the note that they need a mace or hammer in your hand, unless you are a Paladin, shows again (checked in game).

Hunter's Marks are back at their real size: 1.7% more damage taken per Mark. The sim had dropped to 1.4% when patch 90 reworded the support's text. Builds that mark with their own hits (Hunter's Focus, Hunter's Creed, Starmarked Quarry, the Hunter's Mark gem) read a few percent higher.
Hunter's Mark on a summon gem: the army's Marks count again, for the minions and for your own skills (17% more damage taken at 10 Marks). They had dropped out with the same patch 90 text change.
Executioner: its bonus counts below half life again, as its text says. The sim had fallen back to 35% of life, so skills with Executioner read 2 to 4% higher.

Orbit: a projectile sent at an enemy already struck this cast now deals 90% less damage (attacks 97% less), as the support's text says since patch 90 (was 75% and 90%). Orbit skills on a single enemy read lower.

Tree optimizer (Optimize tree, Plan next points, Plan tree) is much faster: a 93-point tree that took about 5 minutes now takes about 20 seconds, and most runs finish in a few seconds. Results are the same or better.

Tree optimizer: it now offers every node the sim says adds damage for your skill, not a fixed list of stats. New picks: freeze duration (Crack), chill effect, Area, chains, minion speed and minion cap, totem count and speed, and a Dwarven Rune Socket for a rune that has none.

Tree optimizer: with a summon as the skill, minion damage notables are now offered and can be moved (before they were always left where they were). Notables with a trigger (Fletcher's Focus, Endless Edge) or a granted support that only adds to the skill (Hunter's Focus, Ossuary Choir) are offered too.
Optimize tree can now reach for a strong notable or cluster further away by refunding your weakest nodes for it. Plan with 6 or more points checks the same and then puts its picks in order again.

Tree optimizer fixes: a tree with nodes no longer linked to the class start (a save from before the tree changed) spends those points again and says so; Plan tree on an empty tree with Dwarven runes worn now finds picks; a run stops after 2.5 minutes and shows the best tree found so far.
Passive tree tooltips: minion damage lines are no longer listed under "Not in the DPS number" while a summon is the skill (the same for totem lines with a totem skill).
Dragonling Aspect: a save that stores the Aspect in lower case ("void") is now read as that Aspect. Before, it counted for nothing.
FAQ: new Site Change History section (About this site) lists every update note the site has shown, newest first, with a search box.

Attack speed from Dexterity (1% per 10) now counts only while Dexterity is your highest attribute, as in the game since patch 91. A hero with more Strength than Dexterity gets none, though the game's Dexterity panel still lists it (checked in game: the skill sheet and a fight both leave it out). Dexterity's evasion is unchanged.

Dwarven runes now need a socket: a worn Dwarven rune counts only while it sits in a Dwarven Rune Socket on the passive tree (or in a Deep-Forged item). A rune with no socket shows "No socket on the tree: not counted" on the Character tab.

Passive tree: Dwarven Rune Sockets look like the game's. Click a taken socket to set or change its rune; Shift-click refunds it (on touch: Set rune in the panel under the tree). Each rune keeps the socket it has in your save.
Tree optimizer: new Dwarven Sockets box. Enter how many sockets you want and Optimize / Plan path to them (Optimize may refund spares). The result says how many your runes need.
The Wyrmling's Second Heart: its Aspect effect now also raises the Dragonling nodes' Aspect lines (Heartscale, Wyrm's Heart), as the game's character sheet shows (checked in game).
The Falling Feather: two rings now raise Fuse Arrow's skill panel number too (the second burst was only counted against the enemy). Two rings add up: x2.0 with two 50% rings (checked in game).

Arrow Totem with Trap: the skill is a totem, not a trap. Trap Support's own damage still counts, but Trap lines from the tree, Oaths and gear (Hidden Edge, Oath of the Snare, Oath of the Hidden Wire) no longer do (checked in game: crit and damage match).
Skill panel DPS now includes Crack for skills that deal Cold damage, as the game's own tooltip does (checked in game).

Conversion: a skill's own conversion (Fuse Arrow, Lightning Arrow and other elemental attacks) now happens first, then Ice, Zap and other conversion lines convert what is left. Passive tree conversion (Hoarfrost Temper) now converts every damage type like a support. Element splits now match the game (checked on Fuse Arrow and Lightning Arrow, patch 91).
Bina's Spotter's Helm: ramp up to 25% (patch 91).
Spell Echo on a Spell Totem: the note now says the game's panel counts the echoes too (checked in game).
FAQ: the Entropy card shows monster chaos resistance at Rupture 100, 160 and 200, and at Riven Tiers.
Skill Scaling: "How to make it stronger" on each card is now folded; click it to open.

Minions now get half of every damage engine line, not only the defence ones: Boundless Mind's Intelligence line, Oath of Many Fires' mana line, cast speed, item Oaths and Bloodlust. Half for the defence lines and for Boundless Mind is checked in game; the rest follow the same rule.
Pyre Spark: its more damage per 100 life is the Grave Golem's own multiplier, not part of the damage engine (checked in game: x1.374 on the golem with 2,875 life; the sim had x1.354).
Skill Scaling: every skill card has a "How to make it stronger" list (which damage lines, attribute, speed, cooldown, crit and ailments raise it), read from the sim's own rules.
Added damage on attacks now uses each attack's own effectiveness (for example Wheeling Axe 60%, Leap Slam 150%). Leap Slam's hit now matches the game exactly (checked in game).
Strength block: the 2% / 4% / 6% block at 100 / 200 / 300 Strength is counted.
Unique lines with tiny saved rolls are no longer rounded wrongly (for example The Patient Bastion).

The skill panel's Ignite number now includes crits, as the game's own tooltip does (patch 90): Pyre of Faith, Consecrated Ground and Orbiting Hammers panels now sit within 0.2% of the game (were about 2% under). Damage against enemies is unchanged: ailments still don't take crit.
Orbiting Hammers: a note says the hit rate is counted for an enemy right next to you; from farther away the ring hits less often (checked in game: about 95% touching, about 75% at 3.7 m).
Anvil of Heaven: checked in game. It bursts on every 6th hit for the part of the hit that strikes; with the Chaos support the burst lays no Entropy.

New Advanced tab in the Build Planner: every number behind your build (speed, crits, hit damage, enemy, mana, attributes, life, energy shield, armour, evasion, resistances, max hit). Hover a dotted row to see which lines make it up.
Advanced replaces Damage Analysis: Damage Composition, DPS Scaling and the modifier lists and notes are there now. Top Optimization Suggestions moved to the Character tab, under the Potions belt.
The site has its own tab icon (the LILSHRIMPER sigil).
Rain of Bolts: the Ballista splash now counts against a single target (checked in game).
Golem blessings: Intelligence's minion bonus is counted once, not twice (checked in game).
Vows: an idol's +1 count line (+1 Ballista, Spark, Chain ...) is no longer offered as a Vow.
Far Shot, Point Blank, Hunter's Mark, Sigil Surge and Arcane Overflow no longer count for skills placed by Spell Totem or Arrow Totem, as their texts say.
Dragonling tree: clicking a node away from your path takes it with the shortest path.
Skill tree tooltips: totem lines that add nothing say why, and a few repeated or -0% lines are fixed.
FAQ: new Entropy card under Ailments.
Skill tree tooltips: Venom Mark and the other "for each Fury / Mark / Ignite" lines the sim counts are no longer listed under "Not in the DPS number".
Skill tree tooltips: when taking a node costs several points, the tooltip names the nodes on the way, since its value counts them too. Thanks for the report.

Vows on red items: since patch 90 the game changes a Vow when the red item already has the same kind of line (a Cast Speed Vow on Cinderwick, which has its own Cast Speed, becomes Cooldown Recovery when you log in). The Add a Vow lists and Optimize this item no longer offer such Vows, and one already on an item now says which line the game turns it into. Thanks for the report.
Optimize tree and Plan tree now also try every Dragonling Aspect and recommend the best one; the switch shows each Aspect's gain, and Apply and Undo set it.
Dragonling tree: hover an Aspect to see what it does; the Aspect is now picked with buttons, each showing what switching to it does to your DPS.
Dragonling tree: every node shows its DPS gain (in its tooltip and as heat map colours), with a Best next picks list you can click to take.
Dragonling tree: the mouse wheel now changes the Dragon Ruptures box.
Optimize tree, Plan tree and Plan next points now spend your Dragonling points too (Plan Dragonling box, on by default). The Aspect you picked is kept.
Database: New first sits on its own row and looks clearly different when on. Clicking the category you already picked goes back to All.

Eyrie Watch (Dragonling, Stormwing): Ballistas last 60% longer, multiplied with your other duration lines, as the game shows. A longer life raises the Bina's Spotter's Helm ramp. Its "placing one at your maximum refreshes them all" did not happen in a game test, so it is not counted.
Gear Set Sim: each changed slot has an Equip button, so you can take one piece at a time and keep the result on screen.
Skill tree tooltips: lines the sim does count (more mana, speed and totem lines, ignite stacks and others) are no longer listed under "Not in the DPS number".

Bina's Spotter's Helm: the 2% more per shot in a row is now counted per Ballista and starts again for every new Ballista, as a test in the game showed. The sim averages it over a Ballista's life, so totem duration and totem speed raise it (attack speed does not). It was a flat 50% more; most builds now get between about 20% and 45%.
With The Unfallen Ancestor your Ballistas never expire, so the helm's ramp counts the full 50%.

Rime Sprites, Cinder Mites and Brass Sentinels now count "+1 to maximum number of minions" lines (like the Core Touched minion amulets): one more companion and 3% more damage of its element each, as the game shows.
Translations: the Market, Vows and Riven Atlas tabs, the newer Item Simulator options, the Damage tab stats panel and the FAQ card on ailment damage are now in all ten page languages.
Patch 90: critical strikes no longer make Bleeding, Ignite or Poison bigger (the game's patch notes). Hits still crit; the ailment numbers drop for crit builds.
Patch 90: a Guardian's freeze bar is now 20% of its life every time (it was 12%, each next bar 50% bigger), so freeze-based helpers and Frostbreak count more Brittle windows.
Patch 90: increased Vow effect from gear and the tree now adds to the Vow's own bonus instead of multiplying it, as the game does now.

Passive tree: Oath of the Pyre, Oath of the Long Night, One Breath, Hammer of Judgement and 9 other nodes no longer show their bursts and sky swords under "Not in the DPS number": the sim counts them (the last update meant to do this but missed).
Passive tree: nodes you marked keep are green now whether you have them or not (taken ones were gold), so a node you want no longer looks forgotten after Apply.

Oath of the Long Night: its frost burst (every third Cold hit, 50% of the hit) is now in the DPS, also when the Cold comes from conversion (Chain Lightning with Ice), as the game's character sheet counts it.
Passive tree: bursts and pillars the sim counts (Oath of the Pyre, Hammer of Judgement, One Breath and others) are no longer listed under "Not in the DPS number".

Conversion: damage converted from one element to another (Lightning to Cold with Ice or Stormfrost, Lightning to Fire with Flame, and so on) now gains the new element's "more" lines too, as the developer's rule file says. Example: Oath of the Long Night on Chain Lightning with Ice is worth about +20% instead of +8.5%.

Gear Set Sim and Sim by Slot: every gear level now tries weapons and armour at 30% quality on Truesworn bases (Base Grade 100); Ashen bases at their 10% cap. Uniques no longer get a Base Grade, as they roll none.
Passive tree: nodes marked must take now show a green ring and flag, apart from the gold keep marks.
Dragonling: the first crown is free, each further crown costs 3 points, and you can hold several crowns, as the game’s tooltips show.
The Wyrmling’s Second Heart now raises your Dragonling Aspect’s lines (it did nothing in the sim before).
Patch 90 red unique lines are in the sim from their texts (not checked in the game yet): Split Aspect, Sentence of the Ninth Bell, Eighth Blade Ornament and Ninth Hammer Shard.
Gear Set Sim: idols the search picks now go where the set fits when you Equip it; a worn red idol no longer pushes another idol out ("No room in the Fossil").
Stats panel: hover boxes now list every line instead of stopping at "... and N more"; long lists show in two columns.
Dragonling: the new Void Aspect has its own dragon picture on the Dragonling button (deep violet), and the Arcane dragon is a paler lavender so the two purples tell apart.

Patch 90: the five Entropy supports (Entropic Focus, Hastened Ruin, Gathering Dark, Cascading Ruin, Pact of Ruin) are in the game now. They are back in the normal support picker, the support search, the support optimizer and the Save Creator.

Item window: against a Guardian, when your other skills fill its freeze bar, a new "View change as kill speed" box beside the prefixes and suffixes shows each line's effect on how fast the Guardian dies (your skill plus those skills) instead of your skill's own DPS. A line that only helps the other skills (more chill on Frost Nova, say) could show a tiny loss before; as kill speed it shows the gain.
Shield Throw: the bonus from your shield’s armour, evasion and energy shield now counts the shield’s Base Grade, as the game does (checked in game: it adds to your other increased damage).
Skills with both Trap and Skyfall linked (Shield Throw, Wheeling Axe ...) now get your increased Skyfall damage lines, as the game’s character sheet shows.
The five Entropy supports other than Chaos are marked as not in the game yet: they sit in their own group in the support picker and are left out of the support search.

Item pictures: 9 new uniques from patch 89 show their own art, and 5 Primal uniques (Webspinner Gloves, Shadowsilk Wraps, The Long Battery, The Third Thunder, The Thousand Sparks) now use their own picture instead of the base item's.
Item Search: the "Might not be obtainable" tag on unique cards now explains itself when you hover it.
Gear Set Sim and Sim by Slot no longer make rares on Ashen bases (the Forge cannot craft on them); Ashen bases are still used for Oathwords and uniques.

Gear Set Sim and Sim by Slot also try each unique on the Core Touched bases of its kind (the Cube's Vowbinding: the Mark) and keep it there when that scores higher. Not when runes are limited below Tier V or Core Touched items are switched off.
A unique you pick now starts with every line at its top roll and 30% quality on weapons and armour (10% on Ashen bases, the game's cap). Both can still be lowered in the item window.
Patch 89: Ember Spark, Rime Spark and Venom Spark can take Trap Support, and Earthshatter can take Skyfall, as the game allows.
Patch 89: unique line strengths updated from the game (Thornwake's more bleed damage is halved, Twinscar changed, three new uniques).
Skill Scaling: the late gem-level damage (levels 18-24) is now in the numbers and listed on each card; levels past 20 read their ramps with gear levels, as the sim does.
Necromancer minions deal 2% more damage per Rupture Level past 160, as the game does (x1.80 at Rupture 200).
Trapped and totem skills: their bleeds are no longer cut by the trap and totem sharing rule (game rule since patch 86).
"Gain X as extra" now reads the damage before conversion (game rule since patch 87), so skills that convert their damage gain a little.
Fortified's "more damage per stack" now adds together with the other "more per stat" lines, and Pyre Spark's golem bonus per 100 life is counted.
Skill Scaling: sort the skills by flat damage (spells) or damage effectiveness (attacks) at any level from 1 to 40; the picked level is marked on each card.
Skill Scaling: skills the newest patch changed get a "Changed in Patch" tile; click it for that skill's change history.

Recent Patch: new uniques that come in many versions (Hands of the Gemwright, Oathstone of the Nameless King, The Split Aspect) show once, with how many versions there are, instead of filling the list with the same name.
Patch 89: Summon Skeletons and Raise Zombie get their 25% more damage at gem level 20 (the late gem-level numbers now come straight from the public API).
Patch 89: Bladesong and Maelstrom on a bow no longer get their melee-only Physical lines (Bladesong on a bow keeps 24% increased Physical Damage, as the patch says). Melee weapons unchanged.
Patch 89: Dread and increased curse effect now add together instead of multiplying, so cursed enemies take a little less from builds with both.
Game data for game build 89. Fixes the page breaking on characters with an Oathword after the new game data arrived.
Vows: a red item only offers Vow lines its own base can roll (no staff lines on wands, no other idol sizes' lines on red idols). Gear Set Sim's idol search also tries red idols with Vows.
Item window: switching the base of a magic, rare or Oathword item keeps every line; lines the new base can not roll are marked.
Mana: your minions now hold mana as in the game (Skeletons and golems 7%, Skeletal Mage and Zombie 5% for a Necromancer), never taking your last 10%. Woebringer auras now reserve their 24% each.
Vows, Curses, Sentences tab: a Woe you link to Woebringer keeps it on its card and shows the mana it reserves.
Vows, Curses, Sentences tab: cards stay in place when you click them (your bar's skills first, then A to Z), and a full bar now shows a clear red warning on the card you clicked.
Grave Call now counts in your minions' DPS while it is on your bar (its minion attack speed). Its tick box can still turn it off. Not checked in game yet.

Vows: a red item can now hold up to 11 Vows (was 6), as in the game. Each later Vow counts less, but a +3 skills line still gives +3 as the 2nd Vow, so the Vow search now tries every order and can put another line first. Gear Set Sim tries 3 Vows when its box is empty, 4 on BiS.

Vows, Curses, Sentences tab: tick a card to add it to your build DPS, click a skill on the bar to take it off, mana and DPS update as you change them. Cards show the gem's attribute need and its tooltip.
Stats panel: a new Entropy section for skills and minions.
Click the build name to change its class and level too. A loaded save character offers to save a copy as a new build instead.
Character tab and Save Creator: ring, amulet, helm, gloves, boots and belt art is centred like the weapon and body armour.
FAQ: a new "Tips for the site" section with a link to the video playlist.

Gear Set Sim and Sim by Slot: a new "Oathsworn rares" box gives each rare the search makes its Oathsworn line from the Cube (a 7th line at the best tier for its item level). On for Endgame and BiS, off for Midgame.

Optimize this item: a new "Riven lines" box lets the search use Riven lines, Vows on red items included. Vows are now picked at item level 84 (the rare they come from), so a red item below 84 can get top-tier and Riven Vows too.
New Build Planner tab: Vows, Curses, Sentences. Your skill bar with a DPS card for each Vow, Herald, Woe and Sentence, their mana cost, and Oath Unbroken and support switches.

Character tab: a Test slot sims one more skill as if it were on your bar, and skills off the bar show their DPS as your main skill. With 13 skills on the bar, "Compare a new skill" puts one next to your main skill.
Potions: the prefix, suffix, Oath and Core lists work like the item window's affix list: type to search, each line's DPS gain, and the roll weight of prefixes and suffixes (not checked in game).
War Banner now counts when it is on your skill bar (its "takes more damage" tick follows the bar like curses), and its skill card on the Character tab shows the damage it adds.
Potions: each line in the prefix, suffix, Oath and Core lists shows how much DPS it adds to your Damage tab skill, like the item window does.
Gem Levels (Skills tab): hover over (or tap) a skill or support gem to see its tooltip.

Gem Levels (Skills tab) is now a chart: when you can get gems (starting gems, the Gemwright at Rupture Level 5, the early gem gifts, Oath Gifts), each class's skill gems as icons with a class switch, and supports grouped by the level they drop from.
Character tab: each skill on the bar now shows how much damage it adds to your counted skills, as a %. The main skill has none.
Character tab: the Skills card shows the skills on your bar; a button shows the rest.
Only skills on your bar add to the sim now. A ticked skill taken off the bar stops counting until it is back.
Skills on your bar with Cast on Crit and nothing linked now always count, as they fire by themselves.
Curses follow your bar: taking a curse skill off the bar unticks its curse on the Damage tab, putting one on ticks it.
Defiant Roar: a war cry with it on your bar now counts 5 Fury charges held. Checked in game (one Fury per roar, up to 5).

New Gem Levels view in the Skills tab: when each support socket opens, what each gem level needs (hero level, attribute, mana) and each class's starting gems. Skills and supports have no unlock levels of their own. Player request.
Character tab: each support on a skill now shows its socket number.
Support Gem Simulator: says when a spell is cast by a channel's Conduit and so uses the channel's supports, with a link to switch.
Ballistas and Arrow Totems: The Long Battery now counts only the Ballistas and totems that can stand (7, or 8 with the Siege Line rune), not every "+Totem" line past that. Player report.
Checked in game: Ballistas and Arrow Totems share a limit of 7, the Siege Line rune raises it to 8, and each count past it gives 5% more damage. The DPS card note now says so.
Plan next points: no longer stops at 60 points; it can plan every point you can still get (level 100 plus Quartz, minus what you have taken).
Spell Totems and Arrow Totems now count Multiple Totems and "+N Totems" lines (they always counted one totem before). The DPS card shows how many Ballistas or totems it counts as standing.
Haemorrhage: new Configure Enemy setting "Enemy bleeding from another skill" (Auto / Yes / No). Auto works as before.
Item window: new "Optimize this item" button picks the best lines for that one item (or the best Vows on a unique, with a box for how many).
Item window: Undo (and Ctrl+Z) per item, one Add list with prefixes on top and suffixes below, and the window fits without scrolling on most screens.
New Stats column beside the Character and Passive tree views: offence, defence and enemy numbers from the sim; hover a row to see the lines behind it.
Tabs always open on their first view: Build Planner on Character, Item Simulator on Item Compare, Skill Scaling on Scaling. The page no longer reopens the last tab.
Sim by Slot keeps items that leave another worn item short of an attribute, with a note.
Best Rivenstone: Vows on uniques are no longer offered. The Forge does not let a Rivenstone work on a unique (checked in the game).

New Best Rivenstone tool in the Item Simulator: it tries every line on your gear that can take a Rivenstone and lists them by what they add. Enter how many stones you have to get the best lines for all of them.

Hunter's Mark Support now fits minion skills (Summon Skeletons, Raise Zombie and the rest), as the game allows: half of the minion blows lay a Mark, and with 10 Marks the enemy takes 17% more damage from you and all your minions (in-game Guardian debuff). Before, the page called it "needs Bow" and counted it as an empty socket.
Energy Shield now counts "N% of your Evasion is added as Energy Shield" (Spirit-Silk Kimono): that share of your total Evasion, added after your Energy Shield increases, as the game's tooltip shows.
Item lines with a negative value now use the game's own wording, e.g. "Energy Shield Recharge starts 20% sooner" instead of "starts -20% later".
Database: uniques that never drop at random and have no known source now say "Might not be obtainable" (was "Does not drop").

Two-handed Oathwords (Bladesong): the weapon's own power lines (its physical damage) now count once, as the game does since patch 88; the +skill level line still counts twice. Bladesong bows and swords show and deal less (thanks to the player who reported it).
Fixed: loading some Mage saves with a Conduit-linked spell failed with "Maximum call stack size exceeded".

Database: Gnome-made, Core Touched and Ashen bases can be found by typing their kind in the search box ("gnome" finds the 6 Gnome-made rings, amulets and belt), and a new Base kind filter (Plain, Core Touched, Ashen, Gnome-made) sits on Uniques, Item bases and All.

EHP: block lines that need a shield or two weapons (Oath of the Aegis, Oath of the Bulwark, Shield Bash, Shield Wall, Twin Discipline) now count when you hold one, and "% of Physical Damage taken as Fire, Cold and Lightning" notables (Tempered Hide and the like) now count: that part of a physical hit meets your Fire, Cold and Lightning resistances instead of armour. The max hit table follows it, and the tree heat map and gear searches now value these when weighing defence.

Arrow Totem, Spell Totem and Ballista: your own attack or cast speed no longer adds damage to them. When your speed was past a skill's cap, the planner turned the extra into damage even when a totem was using the skill, though a totem fires on its own clock. Builds like Hoarfrost Volley with Arrow Totem and high attack speed show less DPS now (about 12% on a player's build), and attack speed lines no longer show a gain for them.

Uniques now show their Red Tier (I to IV), as the game's Collection does: it goes by the level a unique drops from, and the Cube's red recipes use it. Tooltips, the Database, the Market and the Character tab's item window show it and can filter by it (it replaces the base tier shown in the last update).

Uniques now show the Tier the game puts on their card (Tier 1 = the best base of its kind) in their tooltips and cards, and you can filter by it in the Database, the Market and the Character tab's item window.

The old unique "Tier" filter (Standard, Signature, Core, Primal, Chase) is now called Kind, and the Market and the Character tab's item window have it too, with Chase, Primal and Core marks on Market listings.

Entropy (Chaos support and the Chaos keystones): implosions are about 25% bigger. The game lays Entropy from your hit before the general hero damage cut (x0.8), and crits lay crit-sized Entropy (both checked in the game log). Hallowed ground and Unravel no longer raise implosions: they count on hits only, and Entropy is not a hit.
Skill panel numbers with Entropy now match the game's tooltip, which counts the laid share at its implosion size.
Recent Patch: the TLDR now has an entry for patch 87, including the higher Vow rune costs.

Game hotfix of 23 Nov (still build 88): the game's own scaling of red lines changed, and the planner now follows it. Rimecrown Staff (its second line much lower, its first line x1.5), Cinderwick (primal) higher, and new scales on Heart of the White Silence and the primal Wintercall Orb, The Thousand Sparks, Orrery of the Long Night and Charnel Bell (from the game log).

Skill tooltips: the Conversion line now names the damage types a skill converts and shows with an example how its own conversion and conversion from supports and gear are scaled down together when they add up to more than 100%.

Storm Spark and Winter Orb cast by a Channel Conduit: their Sparks and icicles now strike on their own clock while you channel. Before, the planner counted only the conduit's casts, so these builds showed about 1% of their damage (checked against the game log on the Training Post).
Convergence is no longer counted for Sparks cast by a Channel Conduit: each conduit cast replaces the Sparks, so they never build it (game log, 22 Nov).

Patch 88: Chaos damage. The Chaos supports, the chaos keystones and the chaos reds now lay part of each hit as Entropy, which implodes as Chaos damage. It ignores Armour and elemental resistance and shows as its own "Entropy (Chaos)" row. Woe of Entropy raises it. First version, from the patch texts, not checked in a fight yet.

Patch 88 golems: Grave, Flame, Ice, Storm and Venom Golem are separate gems, each with its own blessing whatever its supports. The Grave Golem's blessing gives no damage now. The Storm Golem's shock and the Ice Golem's chill count for you and your minions.

Patch 88 late gem-level damage from the game's own table: Death Coil, Venom Spark, Ember Bolt, Winter Orb, Rime Spark, Fuse Arrow, Lightning Arrow, Pyre of Faith, Cyclone, Thousand Cuts, Flurry and others go up. Judgement (about 46% less at gem 20) and Storm Brand go down.
Tear now cashes at most 4 seconds of a Bleed (patch 88).

New red lines counted: Overclock Coil, The Long Battery, the item Oaths (counted at their full 10%), Arcanist's Overflow, The Bastion Psalm, The Third Thunder, Halo of the Restless Saint (counted standing still), The Falling Feather, Pyreheart Signet, "your crits always Poison / Ignite / Bleed", Bonebreaker Wraps, Lightsworn Reliquary and The Ossuary Lantern.

Brewery: the "of the ... Answer" potion lines now count at the share the game data gives them. Before patch 88 that was half, which explains our 16 Nov test; since patch 88 it is 10-33%, so these potions add much less damage.
Guardian life now runs to Rupture 180 from new game logs (Rupture 180 is a Gate).

FAQ: the damage-engine list comes from the game data (patch 88 kept one tree node per defence). Reds drop from monster level 35. The first Catacombs clear pays Gloomsilver. Recent Patch has a build 88 summary, and the new golems and reds have their icons.

Pyre Burst now counts the share of the corpse's life it deals as Fire (10% at gem level 1, 20% at level 20). The corpse's life follows the game's own corpse table: it grows with the Rupture Level up to 150, and pack life is left out against a Guardian.
Kindled Remains is counted: its corpse bursts need Gravesown's Husks or the new "Fresh corpses a second" setting.
Configure Enemy has a "Corpse" setting for these skills (normal, magic or rare monster, Husk, none).
First version: corpse life is from the game log, but how your damage lines and crits act on the burst is not checked in a fight yet (taken as not raising it).
Gear Set Sim: "plain bases only" now also leaves out Gnome-made bases.
A skill on Arrow Totem or Spell Totem with Trap also linked now counts as a Trap skill, as in the game: Hidden Edge, Oath of the Snare and other Trap lines apply to it.
Skill tree optimizer: it now also chooses which Oath to swear at each Oath seat.

Patch 87: enemies past Rupture 100 resist Fire, Cold and Lightning a little more (0.05% per Rupture Level, up to 10%), as the game log shows. The sim counts it for the Rupture Level set in Configure Enemy.

New patch 87 unique lines now count: crits against Chilled enemies, Ignites on Guardians, the bonuses against Sentenced enemies, spell crit under Woe of Faltering, Herald effect per Herald, and "maximum Energy Shield is 0". They follow the item texts and are not checked in the game yet.
The Chaos support shows a note: Entropy is switched off in the game for now, so it changes nothing.
The three new Guardians (Shellback Tyrant, Drowned Captain, Weaver Queen) are in the Guardian lists with their signature runes.
FAQ: new Vow rune costs, the Cube's idol recipes, and resistance past Rupture 100. Brewery: the Imbue price.
Loot Filter: quivers count with shields and foci, plus the new Quivers, Dwarven Runes and Vow effect options.
Ladder: an open hero shows the build's name in the game's own format, for example "Chain Lightning Mage (Oath of the Snare)".
Ladder: a note says the rank order and hero list come from the public API and can differ from the in-game ladder.
Bastion's Reckoning counts again: only your best defence (Armour, Evasion, Energy Shield or Life), as in patch 87. Since the patch 87 game data it gave nothing in the sim.

Question chat: a few invited accounts see an Ask button that answers questions about the sim and their character (it can run the sim and read the game data). Nobody else sees anything. The privacy page has a section on what it sends.

Conversion: a skill's own conversion (Lightning Arrow, Hoarfrost Volley, Fuse Arrow and the other elemental attacks) now takes every damage type, not only Physical, and shares its 100% with conversion supports and gear, as in the game (Lightning Arrow + Ice leaves no Physical or Fire). Fuse Arrow and Lightning Arrow builds with conversion supports lose some damage in the sim.
Physical converted by a support (Ice, Flame, Zap) now gains the new element's more lines, such as Elemental Focus (game check: x1.547 on Hoarfrost Volley).
Skill tooltips and the Skill Scaling cards show each skill's conversion, and the tooltip lists what your supports, gear and Heralds add. The Damage tab's breakdown shows the conversion step.
Skill tooltips: gear and tree levels give attacks x1.03 each (the old text said about 1% past 5).
Chill: increased chill effect now raises chill up to 50% (it stopped at 30% before), as the game's Chill tooltip says. At 50% chill the enemy takes 35% more damage from hits.

Chill and Brittle no longer raise poison, ignite and bleed ticks (the game's text: ticks do not take them). Builds whose ticks were boosted by chill lose a little damage in the sim. Shock, chill and Brittle still add together.

Idol and Riven lines: the item window, the Build tab and gear tooltips now show these lines as the game does (the game scales some of them, for example idol Ballista and Totem speed x1.3: a 13 reads 17%), with the tier ranges to match. Damage numbers are unchanged; they already counted it.

Shock: the smallest shock now shrinks with how much of the hit is Lightning, as game tests showed. A skill that Ice leaves 40% Lightning shocks a big enemy for about 2.8% (before Shock Effect), not 7%. Lightning skills with Ice or another conversion lose a little damage in the sim; pure Lightning skills are unchanged.
FAQ: the Shock row explains this.
Crack: Damage over Time Multiplier and Freeze Duration now multiply each other on Crack (they used to add), as game tests on the Training Post showed. Cold builds with both deal a few percent more.
FAQ: new Crack section under Ailments, with the test numbers.
Trap with Spell Totem or Arrow Totem: the totem now always places the skill and Trap only adds its damage, whatever order they are socketed in. Before, Trap socketed first was simmed as thrown traps.
Market: Copy search on a listing copies its name to paste into the game's Market ("Name or base" box).
Market: Copy mods on a rare or magic listing copies its three best mods for the game's "Mods" box, so you can find that exact item there.
Market: the "top tier" mark shows from 2 best-tier mods, as in the game.
Market: Live search. Turn it on and the page checks the market every 5 minutes and alerts you when a new listing matches your filters (keep the page open).
Market: find Truesworn bases (Base Grade 90+) with a new mark, a Base Grade filter and a Base Grade sort.
Market: the Riven line mark and filter now say "Riven line (T0)", for searching Tier 0 lines.

New Market tab: search every item listed on the Wagon Market in the public trade leagues, by name, slot, mods, price, weapon and armour numbers and more. You still buy in the game, at the Settler Wagon.
Market: the Upgrade finder sims each listing on your character and shows what it does to your main skill's damage, with sorts for the biggest gain and the most gain for the price.
Market: every search has its own link to share, and listings show the game's marks (Signature, Pinnacle, Riven line, top tier mods).
Rain support: enemies are struck 3 times per use (4 with 4 or more projectiles), and a Ballista's bolts twice, as the support text and the game's skill panel say (the sim used 2 and 3).
Heralds: a hit's extra damage from one Herald is counted once. Damage converted by Ice (or another conversion) used to get it twice.
Hoarfrost Volley: a Ranger can use it at most once every 0.35 s, as the game shows; speed past that turns into damage, as for Split Shot.
Dragonling tree: node names and texts now show in every page language, using the game's own translations.
Dragonling tree: the panel's own labels and hints are translated too. The one-crown-at-a-time rule is confirmed by the game's own text.
FAQ, Damage Multipliers: the developer's stacking table (build 86) now lists the damage engine lines as adding, as the game does.
Dragonling tree: nodes that follow your Aspect show that Aspect's own text, as in the game (Cold Dragon's Heart: Hoarfrost Dive). Crowns show their 3-point cost.
Dragonling tree: the Dragon Ruptures box now shows the points you have earned, and the tree says when your picks cost more than that (not a valid tree in the game).
Recent Patch has a new TLDR view: one patch in plain English (new things, skills that got stronger or weaker, the numbers that moved).
Skill tree tab: the Dragonling panel has a search box. Matching nodes get a red ring and the rest dim.
Dragonling trees now match the game: 43 nodes the game does not have are gone (4 to 10 per class, e.g. Deep Chill and Ink of Stars for Mage). Builds that held one of them lose it, as in the game.
Damage numbers now follow only the game's own data and the current patch notes. Corrections taken from older patch notes are gone:
Piercing Shot, Gravereap, Ballista, Crescent Slash and Rain of Arrows lose an extra late-gem boost the sim added from the patch 79 notes (3 to 21% less).
Pyre of Faith and Unholy Void pulses now set off your on-hit effects again (an old patch 83 note said they did not).
Thunderfall no longer takes your spell damage lines (its current text does not say it does).
New icons for the Gravefeast gem and the Gravesown and Kindled Remains supports. Sworn Surge (was Elemental Overload) shows its new name in damage notes.
Dragonling: the tree is now the patch 86 Ascension 2.0 tree (War and Ward crowns on every path).
Dragonling points now come from Dragon Ruptures cleared (one at each of Rupture Levels 10, 20 ... 200), not from your level or Gates. A crown costs 3 points.
Builds made before patch 86 keep their Dragonling: each node moves to the one that replaced it (a node the new tree dropped is left out).
Save Creator: a Dragonling copied into a save is written for the new tree, so the game keeps it.
Patch 86: ailment chance over 100% now turns into increased ailment damage (125% bleed chance = +25% bleed damage), as the patch notes say. Builds with very high bleed or poison chance go up.
Patch 86: Thousand Feathers now adds into your damage engine instead of multiplying on its own (the developer's formula file). Projectile attack builds with it come down a little.

Patch 86: the tree lines that pay "more damage for each Fury charge, Hunter's Mark, 1% Block, 1% crit chance..." now count, added into your damage engine. Hammer Choir counts at its 12% when Orbiting Hammers is on your bar.

Patch 86 notables now counted: Iron Momentum (moving fights), Elemental Cadence (spells of two elements on your bar), Reed Wind (set movement skills a second in Configure Enemy), Hallowed Stand (standing fights, enemy on hallowed ground).
Aaron's Golemheart: each golem now lends its own blessing (patch 86).
Fixed: some builds with Cast on Crit and Frostbreak froze the page against a Guardian.
The Skills tab under Build Planner is gone: skills are added and edited on the Character page (the skill list on the right).
A link or code pasted into the empty Build Planner now opens on the Character page too.
Share links now open the build on the Character page (gear and stats) instead of the Skills page.
New Home button under the site title (on phones, next to it): it takes you back to the start page with its tool list. The logo opens the Build Planner.
Click a plan's name (at the top of the Build Planner or in Saved Builds) to rename it.
Loot Filter: the new text (sample drops, the fuller item tester, weapon kinds, top grade, undo) is translated in all ten languages.
Loot Filter: filters can now have up to 40 rules, as the game takes (it was 12).

Loot Filter: new "Sample drops" card. Roll random gear through your rules to see how much is shown, highlighted or hidden, and how many drops each rule catches. It is a rough look: how the game rolls drops is guessed.

Loot Filter: the item tester now knows weapon kinds (Bows, Claws, Wands and the rest) and checks the More conditions: tier, sockets, required level, Base Grade, reds, unsworn, named bases and named reds.
Loot Filter: "Top grade" (Under grade 50 / 70 / 90) can be set in More conditions.
Loot Filter: Undo for every change (button or Ctrl+Z), an All / Highlights / Show / Hide switch for long rule lists, and "Copy as text".

The EHP estimate now counts maximum resistance lines (runes, idols, tree, potions; up to 85%), Fortified, Resolve charges, Woe of Faltering and "reduced damage taken" from potions. Hover the EHP number to see what is counted.
Lines that make you take more damage (Glass Cannon and others) now lower the EHP estimate.

Brittle and Frostbreak on a Guardian now start when its freeze bar fills and stop when it dies. Before, short fights counted the Guardian as Brittle from the first second, so fast cold builds read too high (up to about 15%). Long fights are unchanged.
Shock, chill and Brittle now add together (the game's own stacking table and Freeze tooltip). Before, only the strongest of them counted.
A Brittle Guardian takes 10% more damage from every skill's hits for the 5.5 s after its freeze bar fills, not only with Frostbreak.
Chill is now 10% to 30% by the size of your cold hit against the enemy's life (game log), so cold skills deal more on rares.
Increased freeze duration (Stormfrost and others) fills a Guardian's freeze bar faster (game log, 20 Nov).
A Guardian's freeze bar no longer fills when your cold hits land more than 6 s apart. Crack now counts on unique enemies too.

Skill tree: when the picked skill is cast by Cast on Crit, the note under the tree says the source skill's crit chance and attack or cast speed count toward its DPS. When the picked skill holds Cast on Crit, the note says the spell it casts is not counted, with a button to count it too.
Runes on shields and tomes now give their armour-side lines (as on body armour), not the weapon line. Builds with runes in an off-hand shield or tome see their numbers change.
Riven Atlas: new search box (node name or effect); matching nodes get a red ring.
Riven Atlas: clicking a node also takes the nodes before it, and when you run out of points the Rupture Level, then the Riven Tier, goes up to pay for it instead of showing a warning.
Gear Sim: a warning when your rare or magic items have no stat lines (gear from a game build code), since they then count as bare bases.
Database: sort by drop weight (rarest first or commonest first) on Uniques, Item mods, Item bases and All. Cards show their weight while that sort is on.

Guardian life now follows the game's own numbers from its log (target fight time x the game's model DPS x the Deep's life multiplier). This changes shock size, the freeze bar and Kindling a little at most Rupture levels.
FAQ: new Guardian life table on Guardian Fights; The Deep now shows the game's real life and damage multipliers (life x214 at Rupture 150, not x7.9).
FAQ: the Ailments page also shows how ailment damage adds and multiplies; Herald kill effects moved from Drop Chances to Damage Multipliers; number tables no longer have uneven gaps.
Riven Atlas: the Character, Passive tree, Skills and Damage tabs now show above the atlas, so you can leave it again.
New Riven Atlas tab in the Build Planner: plan your Atlas points (drops, experience and monsters; it does not change your damage).
Database: Primal uniques show their Primal tag next to the name, so they are easy to tell apart from the normal unique of the same name.
Database: hover a unique's tag (Signature, Chase, Core, Primal, Limited) to see what it means. Primal items now list all the places they drop from.
Save Creator: the steps no longer say to close the game (only the character must not be logged in), and the offline-only notice and all four steps are translated.
Save Creator: a notice that it is for offline characters only, and a save is now also refused when it carries an online id.

Save Creator: it now remembers the last offline save you picked for each class (kept in this browser only). Paste a build code and it goes onto the remembered save of its class, without picking the file again.

Save Creator: gear and idols are shown like the Character tab, and the bag like the game's own window with the pouch row. Click an empty gear slot, Fossil cell, bag cell or pouch place to add an item there; items open in the same item window as the Character tab.
Save Creator: drag idols and bag items to move them, drop one on an item of the same size to trade places, hold Ctrl to copy an idol. Jewels show their gem.
Save Creator fixes: the bag is 12 cells wide (the page took it as 9), the Dwarven Fossil takes its 2x2 cells so a new item no longer lands on it, and Base Grade is now written to the save.
Dragonling, Cold Heart: Hoarfrost Dive now counts its 50% more on a Guardian that is Frozen, Brittle or past half its freeze bar (from the node text and the game's data, not yet checked in game).
Mana on kill and movement speed on kill are no longer listed as "not modelled".
Gear Sim: Oathwords it recommends now show Craftable when you have the runes in your saves.
FAQ, Forge & Crafting: Gloomsilver is a rare find since patch 84; the Oath Broker sells 5 a day for gold; Lightless Anneal costs 3 Gloomsilver.
Support picker: supports that change nothing for the selected skill now sit in their own "No effect in the sim" group; they can still be socketed.
The new landing page is translated in all ten languages, with the passive tree's Names and Gateways buttons.
Updates now come in two kinds: sim changes, bug fixes and data updates still ask you to refresh; interface changes, translations and small features load by themselves the next time you open a tab.

New landing page: four ways to start (saves, new plan, build code, ladder build), the game data on the page in numbers, every tool as a card with a short description, how the numbers are checked, and the latest site update.
Ladder: EHP now counts evasion too (half the hits taken as attacks), against monsters at the hero's Rupture Level.
Passive tree: new Names and Gateways buttons in the corner show or hide node names and the dotted gateway lines. Your choice is remembered.
Passive tree: names no longer overlap. They stay the same size at any zoom and sit beside their node wherever there is room. More names appear as you zoom in, with taken nodes and search hits first.
Passive tree: taken paths are now thinner gold lines, and each Oath seat is named once instead of twice.
Wands now give spells their crit chance, like staves (the wand's crit takes the place of the 6% spell base). Other local weapon lines still give spells nothing.
Database: clearer text on local weapon crit and attack speed lines about what they do for attacks, spells and minions.
Item Search is now called Database (same address).
Database: item mods now show a Local or Global tag. Hover it to see what that means for the line.

Recent Patch: new Dragonling section with changes to Aspects, each class's Dragonling nodes and Hearts, keystone rules and tree points. Each class has its own dropdown, and keystone rules have one too.
Item Search and the Build planner: icons for the support gems Unravel, Skyward Oath, Stormhound Pact, Pale Apprentices and Rimewake (game art from build 85).
FAQ, Damage Multipliers: damage over time is now two rows, increased ailment damage and the Damage over Time Multiplier, and covers Poison, Ignite and Bleed.
FAQ, Damage Multipliers: a new table shows for every group of damage lines whether they add or multiply, with worked numbers and a list of cases players ask about.

The damage engine ("more damage per 1,000 Armour, per 1% Block" lines) was measured again on game build 85: the lines add to each other. The developer's stacking table says otherwise; this was reported.

Item lines follow the game's build 85 table: Riven damage lines count 85 to 96% of their roll (77 to 89% before), idol physical, elemental, spell, melee and crit lines 75% (50% before), the new 2x2 idol lines in full.
Skill level lines on gear read their full roll again (+3 on a two-hander is +3), and a Vow's +level line no longer counts at half.

Grave Golem: its blessing is at half strength with no increased minion damage or minion life, full strength from 100% of the two together (the gem's text). Heroes without minion lines get less from it than before.

New supports from game build 85 now count: Skyward Oath (2 sky swords at 24% of a crit, once a second), Stormhound Pact (Storm Wolves leaping for 16% of a crit; the spell must be at least a quarter Lightning) and Rimewake (a frost burst for 25% of a movement skill's hit).
Afterimages: the new "Afterimages deal increased damage" lines (Twin Fang Discipline, idols) now count.

The Dexterity keystone (0.5% more per 10 Dexterity) now counts only for Projectile attacks and Rain of Arrows, as the game says since build 85 (bows only before). Until now the page gave it to melee attacks too.
Hammerbearer's Reliquary: its extra orbiting projectile now also counts on skills with the Orbit support. Vows and Heralds now reserve 20% of your mana, as their gem texts say.
Recent Patch: the history of the oldest game builds (from before the public API) was tidied up.
Game build 85 is in: Recent Patch lists everything it changed (skills, supports, Vows, uniques, the new notables, Oathwords and item mods).

Vows: every Vow line is now 15% stronger, as the game has had since Patch 82 (its gem texts show it: Vow of Iron 50.6% more Armour at gem 20). Fervent Vow adds another 15% of the base (Vow of Iron 57.2%). Builds with Vows read about 1-4% higher.

Executioner and Life Leech: their more damage now counts on hits only, not on Bleed, Poison or Ignite (the game's new texts). Executioner still makes ailments count a little more from the kill at 10% life.
Ruthless: its every-third-blow bonus no longer raises the Bleed or Poison it starts (the game's new text).
Skill tree heat map: colours now rank every node against the rest, with a fold-out legend on the right (lowest, median and top gain per point). Opening the legend turns the heat map on.

Heat map marks: red = taking the node lowers your value, dashed grey = a taken node that loses nothing when refunded, dotted = the node has lines the sim does not count. Node values follow the Prioritize slider (DPS or defence).

Oath seats: empty seats are coloured by their best Oath, and a new "Oath seats open" button in the tree's top left jumps to the next empty seat and opens its Oath menu, which now shows the Oaths side by side.

EHP estimate: glancing blows are in (in-game Evasion tooltip). An attack you cannot evade is cut by your evade chance; the EHP hover box shows your evade chance and the biggest physical hit you survive as a glancing blow. The EHP number itself stays the same.

Bleed: Tear now counts. A crit (or any Slam hit) on a bleeding enemy cashes half the bleed still to come, at most once a second; the game keeps 40% of that as extra damage and takes the rest from later ticks (game logs). Most bleed builds gain about 7-12% bleed damage.

Translations: the newer page text (Saved Builds, full screen tree, Windburst, Gather Fury, freeze bar, Base Grade, Elemental Echo and more) now shows in every page language. New items from game builds 83 and 84 keep their English names until the game's language files have them.
Saved builds: moving to another build while the open one has unsaved changes now asks first: Save, Discard or Cancel.

Frostbreak: its 50% more now counts against Guardians. Cold hits fill the Guardian's freeze bar (12% of its life, each next bar x1.5); each fill gives 5.5 s of the bonus, averaged over the fight. A new box on the Damage tab adds the cold from your other skills.

Dragonling: the Gate kills + Pinnacle box now follows the nodes you take, like the level follows passive points. Take more nodes than your level gives and it goes up by itself, to all Gates, the Seal of 80 and the Pinnacle; past that the level goes up to the milestone that holds them.
Dragonling: the panel now fills the tree view, details on the left and the tree beside them, so the whole tree shows without scrolling. The Taken list shows names; hover one for its text.
Passive tree: a Full screen button next to Fit shows the tree over the whole window, with the points count in the corner. Esc or Exit full screen goes back.
Wake of Spells: Channelling skills supported by the tree's Channel Conduit now show the Linked spell box, so you can pick the spell it casts without a Conduit gem in the sockets.

Saved builds: a saved build now changes only when you press Save. Edits stay as unsaved changes (they survive a refresh), a bar at the top offers Save and Discard changes, and Ctrl+S saves. Your account gets the saved build only.
Item window: the Edit tab is wider and in two columns, so a whole item shows without scrolling on a desktop screen.

Item window: each line now shows what it does to your DPS (green +4.51%), on the item and in the Add Prefix / Add Suffix / Add Vow lists. It is the Damage tab skill's total DPS with the line against without it.

Amulets: the suffix "increased effect of your Vows" (17-20% at the top tier) can now be picked and counts; builds wearing it were missing the line. The item level each tier needs is not confirmed yet.
Gather Fury: while the gem is linked to a skill on your bar, the page now counts 2 Fury charges as held (8% increased damage, 4% attack and cast speed each). Before, it counted nothing.
New box "Fury from Gather Fury" under Vows, Heralds & charges (in Configure Enemy) to change that number. If the Fury box is higher, that number counts instead.
Support Gem Simulator: Gather Fury is now a normal choice instead of sitting under Packs and extras.

Necromancer, Spellbound Dead: a quarter of your Fury charges, your untagged increased damage and Intelligence's spell damage now reaches your minions, as in the game (checked against in-game Summon Skeletons tooltips and the game log). Minion builds with this node read a few % higher.

Item editors and Gear Set Sim: magic and rare items now hold at most 2 runes (rares roll at most 2 sockets). Turning a white item magic or rare drops its 3rd and 4th rune; Oathwords keep their own number of sockets. The Endgame and BiS gear levels plan rares with 2 sockets.
Item window: Armour, Evasion and Energy Shield under Implicits now follow the item's Base Grade and Quality (e.g. Evasion 131 (base 105, grade 125%)).
Ticking Truesworn by hand now sets Base Grade 100. Imported items keep their own grade.
Prefixes, suffixes and Vows show their roll chance on the item's base, as Item Search does (e.g. WEIGHT 22% (100/448)), on the item's lines and in the list when adding one.
Ladder: when the game publishes a hero's build empty for a while, the Ladder shows the last full build the site read and says so.
Support Gem Simulator: one column (search, then Configuration, then the gem setup). Vows, Heralds and charges are now in the Configure Enemy window, which looks the same on every page.

Elemental Echo (Vow): with it on your bar, the Vows, Heralds & charges list has a tick box for each echo (Physical, Fire, Cold, Lightning, Poison): 12% more damage of that element. They start unticked, as an echo needs a kill by your own hit.
Your minions get the echo of their element too (checked against in-game Skeletal Mage tooltips: Fire x1.12, Physical unchanged). The Physical Echo is not counted for minions.
Elemental Echo's Vowbreak box now gives its 20% more damage; before, it did nothing.

Minions: a sworn Oath's lines that name only an element (Oath of the Pyre Heart, Frozen Heart, Storm Heart) now count for your minions too, as tree and item lines already did (checked against in-game Skeletal Mage tooltips).
Skill tree search: every matching node and Oath seat now gets a red ring, matching names turn red when zoomed in, and the number of matches shows under the search box.
Minions: the young-gem bonus of a summon gem (Summon Skeletons: up to 30% more below gem level 16) now counts for its minions too.
Summon Skeletons: they attack a little slower, as the game shows (fitted to the game log; Multistrike does not change it). Builds with Skeletons read lower, fast armies the most.
Killer Instinct now counts on minion skills: +4% base crit chance, 100% increased crit chance and +40% crit multiplier for the linked minions.
Minions holding a staff now use the staff's local crit line on their base crit, as the game does (checked against an in-game Summon Skeletons tooltip).

Riven lines: the game counts most offensive Riven lines at 77 to 89% of their roll, and the page now does the same. Riven + gem level lines count in full (Patch 84). A two-handed weapon's +3 gem levels line reads +2, as the game's own table has it.

Guardian life up to Rupture Level 39 now follows the game's own figures on Patch 84 (about twice the old numbers; Gates are much weaker than the Guardians around them). It only changes shock size and Kindling.
Pyre of Faith and Unholy Void: their pulses no longer set off on-hit bursts from the tree and items (Patch 83). Orbiting Hammers on a Necromancer: cast speed past the cap now becomes damage.

"Takes more damage" effects: Woes and Sentences now multiply with each other instead of adding, as the game's own log for Patch 84 lists them as separate kinds. Death Sentence 25% with a 20% Woe is now x1.50 (was x1.45).
Guardians at Rupture Level 22 to 30 have the lower life Patch 84 gave them, read from the game log.
Riven lines are scaled the way the game reads them; from Patch 84 Riven skill level lines count in full.
Necromancer Orbiting Hammers: cast speed past its fastest cast now turns into damage, as for attacks (game log).
Pyre of Faith and Unholy Void pulses no longer set off on-hit effects from your tree and items (Patch 83).

Spells cast through another skill's Cast on Crit link (Venom Spark from Death Coil, for example) now get that skill's fitting supports on the triggered cast, as the game's tooltip says. The panel number stays the hand-cast one the game shows.
Sparks: Convergence is no longer in the panel DPS, because the game's tooltip leaves it out. The numbers against an enemy still count it.
Necromancer: the three Grave Lore points by the start now each add their minion (a Skeleton, a Skeletal Mage or a Zombie), as in Patch 84. The page left them out before.

Patch 84: "takes more damage" effects now follow the new rule. The same kind adds (Woes, Sentences and Unravel; Marks and the War Banner; Maim, the venom golem and hallowed ground) and different kinds multiply. Which kind each effect belongs to is our reading of the patch notes.

Patch 84 numbers: Death Coil, Drain Life, Venom Spark, Skeletons, Skeletal Mages and Zombies use the new high gem level values. An Oathword's power lines count twice on a two-handed weapon again (Nightshade on a staff: +3 levels).

Minions, checked against in-game tooltips: Venom Support converts their damage too, Herald of Rot and the Dragonling's extra poison reach them, your poison-only damage lines count in a new place, Maim is in their DPS, and their crit chance comes from your staff.
Idols: the game counts idol lines at a share of what the Fossil panel shows (generic damage and crit lines half, build lines 30% more). The page now does the same.

Link rule fixes: movement skills lose damage for empty sockets too (Vampire Dash with 2 of 6 deals 43%), and a spell cast through another skill's Cast on Crit counts that skill's fitting supports as links. Movement skill cooldowns stop at 0.3 s.

A Dwarven rune's + gem level line no longer adds a level to skills, Heralds or Vows (the game's tooltips leave it out). Cast speed past a spell's cooldown floor or a channel's fastest tick now becomes damage.
Item editors: new "% of base" box beside Base Grade. Type the % the game shows on the item (Base Grade: 98 Truesworn, 124% of the base) and the page sets the grade; 119% or more ticks Truesworn.
Minions: Glass Cannon now gives every minion 25% more damage (the sim counted nothing from it; checked on the skill panels).
